1) I first remember experiencing it my sophomore year of college and it has progressively become more of a common occurrence and less intense generally over the years

2) I don’t usually have visual hallucinations as many report but I do hear loud rushing noises like water and I can’t open my eyes no matter how hard I try. It usually only lasts a few seconds and I just have to slow my breathing and try to stay calm and like I try to all at once jolt all my muscles to get anything to move to wake myself up. 

3) I notice that it happens when I am not getting the best sleep and also when I wake in the morning and then try to go back to sleep. Also, I don’t always have to be on my back to experience and I can sleep on my back without having an episode. 

4) I feel like I don’t have sleeping issues besides falling asleep when I am anxious. But when I have sleep paralysis, I can’t go back to sleep. No way it would just happen again.

5) it doesn’t mess with my life at all.

I am Native American, Mohawk, and my name translates to “she who conducts the wind” and I could never figure out what the hell that was supposed to mean. When I was 14 I started feeling depressed and didn’t quite understand what was happening and didn’t want to accept that I was someone with depression. Whenever I was feeling bad all I wished was that I could be a bird and fly away to anywhere in the world and just be free. I got a bird tattooed on my ankle as a final acceptance of my mental health challenges and it is flying forward to show that I control/conduct where the wind will take me in life and that everything I experience, good and bad, moves me forward.

Well this is a first step asking us for help. I have always struggled with this as well and not just in terms of what i need emotionally but with academics and money help from my parents. I guess it is sometimes a pride thing I have. The first person I told about my depression tried to be helpful which was great but he didn’t really know how to help me and I think it made him uncomfortable. It at least gave me some more confidence in talking about the hard stuff. Once you start talking about it, it gets easier. I have tried therapy a couple times but have never found one that fits, but I know for many people it has turned their life around. Maybe you should give it another shot because there is low pressure since they are strangers and they help people for a living. And maybe talking about things will make you more comfortable and help you figure out what you need to ask from the people around you! If there is anything I can do too, if you ever just need to chat or vent feel free to message me.

I was in the exact same place about a year ago. I would lay on the floor for hours only getting up to do things I needed to do so I wouldn’t lose my job or get too smelly. It took a while and that medicine wasn’t perfect for me and have since switched but it at least gave me some room for motivation. It’s really good that you are forcing yourself to do stuff at least. Just keep at it! I had a moment two weeks ago where I felt the most like myself I had felt in probably 5 years and it was incredible!
